title: applied-ml-weekly-notes-2026-05-19
content:
Applied ML weekly research notes - 2026-05-19

Attendees: Aisha Patel (owner), Marcus Nguyen, Sofia Martinez, Daniel Kim, Priya Rao, guests: Leah (SRE), Tom (serving-runtime)

High level summary:
- Focus this week: quantization experiments (q8/q4), end-to-end eval pipeline improvements, and onboarding one new candidate model (Mistral-7B-instruct-v0.2).
- Good progress on automated eval artifacts: CI now uploads eval summaries to Confluence + artifact store; still need to attach interactive diffs for failed test cases.
- Performance: q4 paths show strong latency improvements on dedicated GPU pools but we observed a tokenizer mismatch risk on one onboarding flow.

Notes / research updates:
1) Quantization experiments
- Setup: used bitsandbytes q4_0 (static) and q8 on gguf-converted checkpoints for Llama2-13B-alt and Mistral-7B-instruct candidate. Tests ran on p4d and a8g instance classes in Dedicated cluster.
- Key metrics (median of 5 runs):
  - Llama2-13B (fp16 baseline): p50 latency 120ms, p95 340ms, tokens/sec 85
  - Llama2-13B (q8): p50 95ms (-21%), p95 280ms (-17%), tokens/sec 115 (+35%)
  - Llama2-13B (q4_0): p50 58ms (-52%), p95 180ms (-47%), tokens/sec 170 (+100%)
- Quality: ran SummEval subset (n=200) + internal truthbench (n=400). Observations:
  - q8: negligible quality change (ROUGE-L delta < 0.5 on SummEval; accuracy on truthbench within noise).
  - q4_0: small degradation on some long-context summarization cases and code generation (per-case regression ~1.8-3% depending on metric). Perplexity on WikiText2 increased by ~6%.
- Takeaway: q4_0 provides compelling latency/throughput improvements with small but measurable quality regressions on specific workloads. Candidate for serving for high-throughput, high-tolerance products (embeddings, simple chat).
- Follow-ups: run a controlled eval on our regression test-suite (APPL-341) across longer context lengths (>=2048 tokens) to better characterize q4 regressions (Marcus).

2) Evals pipeline improvements
- CI now posts a summary JSON and a human-readable HTML diff to the artifact store (PR: model-zoo/pull/482). Daniel validated uploads for 3 recent runs.
- Still missing: easy per-example diff viewer for non-JSON outputs (e.g., code execution traces). Working with Console UX to add a lightweight viewer.
- New sanity checks: tokenization-consistency check added into onboarding pipeline - fails early if tokenizer produces >1% tokenization-length delta vs baseline. Sofia implemented and pushed test, but saw one false positive on Mistral candidate due to <1% rounding behavior.

3) Model onboarding (Mistral-7B-instruct-v0.2)
- Steps completed this week:
  - Convert from original checkpoint to gguf and create baseline fp16 profile.
  - Run auto-quantize scripts (q8 and q4_0), produce perf profiles.
  - Run unit evals: summarization, instruction-following, safety heuristics.
- Blocker: tokenizer mismatch flagged by new sanity check - trailing special token encoding differs vs our tokenizer bundle, causing ~1.2% perplexity increase. Root cause likely tokenizers version drift (HuggingFace tokenizers 0.15 vs 0.16).
- Action: Sofia to create a small compatibility patch to normalize special-token handling and re-run conversion; if patch fails, fallback is to vendor the tokenizer bundle in model config.

4) Serving-runtime compatibility notes
- KV cache warmup: q4_0 path had ~8% higher p95 until KV cache warms (first 2 tokens). Tom will instrument more detailed per-layer kernel timings to verify whether kernel selection on first call is suboptimal.
- Batching behavior: continuous batching interacts poorly with very short prompts on q4_0 (some extra micro-batching overhead). We should add an autoscaler hint to reduce tiny-batch accumulation for q4_0 models when latency SLOs are strict. Marcus to prototype a dynamic batch-threshold control.

Decisions made this week:
- Enable q8 as the default quantized profile for the Hosted API for mid-tier customers (pilot) - lower risk and good perf/quality balance.
- Keep q4_0 as opt-in for Dedicated customers with documented caveats about corner-case regressions and long-context tests.

Action items
- Marcus Nguyen: run extended regression suite for q4_0 vs fp16 on LongContext tests (>=2048 tokens). Deliverable: spreadsheet + per-case diffs by 2026-05-26. (APPL-341)
- Sofia Martinez: finalize tokenizer compatibility patch and re-run gguf conversion for Mistral candidate. If problem persists, vendor tokenizer in model config. Due 2026-05-22.
- Daniel Kim: add per-example code-exec trace diffs to CI artifact viewer and update PR notes (model-zoo/pull/482). Due 2026-05-24.
- Priya Rao: prepare a short playbook blurb for Support/Oncall describing q4 known issues and recommended routing policies; post to Confluence. Due 2026-05-23.
- Tom (serving-runtime): instrument first-token kernel selection timings and report back with data and suggested mitigations. Due 2026-05-25.

Open questions / risks
- How large is the real-world impact of q4_0 regressions on high-value customers (e.g., agents doing long-form code generation)? Need telemetry-based signal from beta customers.
- Tokenizer drift across upstream model releases - should we pin tokenizers per model and include in model manifests? (Proposal: yes, vendor tokenizers in manifest for Private deployments).

Misc notes / docs links
- PR with artifact uploads and initial viewer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-zoo/pull/482
- Tracking ticket for regression suite extension: APPL-341
- Quant & Eval playbook (draft): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/APPL/pages/123456789/Quant+and+Eval+Playbook

Next week focus
- Finish onboarding of Mistral candidate and get a canary serving endpoint in Dedicated for internal beta.
- Run extended q4_0 regression suite and summarize per-customer-risk guidance.
- Add per-example code execution diffs to artifact UI and finalize playbook for Support.

Meeting adjourned.

Notes-to-self / todo (private): attach raw eval JSONs to Confluence page, request telemetry from two beta customers in Hosted to observe q4 behavior in production, prepare short internal comms about q8 default decision.
